h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A residual on edge 3 keeps the conv-heavy deep path trainable so the added 3x3 capacity on edge 5 is actually realized.
A clean identity bypass on edge 3 lets the deeper 0-1-2 path benefit from an extra 3x3 conv without optimization difficulty.
When edge 5 already supplies a 3x3 conv into node 3, a second parallel conv on edge 4 is partly redundant, giving diminishing returns.
Edge 0 influences the output only through its downstream edges, so a conv there pays off more when edge 2 propagates node 1 through a learned conv.
When edge 0 is identity, node 1 carries no learned features, so edge 1's conv becomes the main transforming source for the node-2 route.
With the deep path cut at edge 5, the direct edge 3 must carry more of the cell's computation, so a conv there matters more.
When the direct route delivers only pooled input, an identity via node 1 restores sharp, unblurred features to the output.
When edge 1's conv already produces rich features at node 2, an identity on edge 5 is an efficient conduit, whereas otherwise edge 5 itself needs to transform.
When edge 1 is removed, edge 2 is node 2's only input, so the operation on it alone determines what flows down the edge-5 path.
A conv on edge 4 keeps learned features flowing into node 3, so the capacity lost by pooling on edge 5 is largely compensated.
